items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: three reeds, one of whom was Ralph LaLama by the way, he was in college at the time at Youngstown State University, that’s where I first met him

ctx.x: How did you arrive at nine?

Well Sam DeAngelo and I had done a band of that size when we were in Youngstown, we did, I used to go back home during the summer to work in factories and whatever, making some money for college. And also, so the summer of 1974 which was just before my senior year in college we decided to put this band together which was basically a nonet plus a vibes player, it was ten pieces. So we came up with a similar instrumentation. It was trumpet, French horn, valve trombone, three reeds, one of whom was Ralph LaLama by…

with like a big band punch if you wanted it, but at the same time it gave you the advantage of being a hip small group when you wanted that as well. And there were a lot of different colors with all the doubles and everything. That was really important, having all those doubles.
